newsitem.title: TAIWAN: POLL-Taiwan June CPI seen rising 1.7 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: POLL-Taiwan June CPI seen rising 1.7 pct yr/yr.

text.p: A Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists on Thursday projected that Taiwan's consumer price index for June would show a year-on-year rise of 1.7 percent.
The official figures were to be issued at 0300 GMT on July 5 by the cabinet's Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics.
May's CPI growth was 0.75 percent year-on-year.

Economists said they expected June's consumer prices to have risen signicantly compared with prevous months mainly due to torrential rains that hit the island in June, especially early in the month, driving up fruit and vegetable prices.
In the first five months, Taiwan's CPI grew 1.27 percent year-on-year.

"The early June floods, according to official figures, had severely damaged vegetables and caused vegetable prices sharply up 81 percent compared with early May prices," said Grand Cathay Securities economist Chang Jui-hsing.
"But aside from sharp rises for food prices, other consumer prices should be pretty stable, following the recent trend," said HSBC James Capel economist Stephen Wang.
The cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development has set a 1997 CPI growth target of 3.0 percent.
In March, the central bank revised its forecast for 1997 CPI growth to around 3.0 percent from 3.31 percent.
